Marcus / Lauren / Jordan — thanks for the context and the documents. Quick legal read below with proposed redline snippets you can paste into the MSA: 

1) Confidentiality window
Proposed: "Except for aggregate or anonymized metrics, Confidential Information disclosing Customer-specific business metrics shall remain confidential for a period of twenty-four (24) months following disclosure or until termination of the Order Form plus twelve (12) months, whichever is shorter."
Rationale: preserves limited-term confidentiality while protecting Redwood's right to retain system-level metrics for operations.

2) Publicity / logo use
Proposed clause: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable license to display Customer's name and logo solely for Redwood's marketing materials, website partner pages, and case studies, subject to Customer's prior written approval for any press release or quoted testimonial. Email approval from an authorized representative shall satisfy this requirement. Any logo use must comply with the Customer's provided logo specification."
Add: a "non-endorsement" sentence: "Use of Customer's marks shall not imply endorsement beyond factual partnership acknowledgment."

3) Makegood / quote fallback
Proposed: "If a promised quote or testimonial becomes unavailable through no fault of Redwood, Redwood may request to publish a jointly approved case study or a customer-approved excerpt within six (6) months of the original publication date; Customer's written approval shall not be unreasonably withheld."
Limit: suggest limiting to one makegood instance per fiscal year to avoid open-ended commitments.

4) Operational asks for Marketing
Marketing will need the logo package and brand guidelines (requested file avatech_logo_spec.pdf). Please confirm an approved contact and preferred file format.

Jordan — if those redlines look broadly acceptable we can prepare a marked MSA + suggested Order Form language and return it by EOD tomorrow.

— Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

- Confidentiality: 24 months is OK, but we need the language to be tied to identifiable categories. We'll accept the shorter of 24 months or termination + 12 months only if we can carve out aggregated system metrics explicitly.
